title: Application windows appear on second monitor task manager when dragging it near the bottom edge on main monitor.
line: A window near the bottom of a screen now stays in that screen's task manager instead of jumping to a lower neighbouring screen.
explanation: On Wayland, libtaskmanager decides a window's screen from its centre point. When the centre is on no screen (a window hanging off the bottom of a screen whose neighbour sits lower), it took the screen with the nearest corner, which can be the neighbour even though the window is only visible on the first screen. Task managers set to show only the current screen then listed it on the wrong screen. The change picks the screen showing the largest part of the window and keeps the nearest-corner rule only for windows entirely off-screen.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: Put a window on the screen showing most of it

A window whose centre was on no screen went to the screen with the nearest
corner, so a tall window hanging off the bottom of one screen could show up
in a lower neighbour's task manager. Pick the screen with most overlap.

BUG: 512147

media.caption: Master: Konsole sits at the lower right of the left screen (right screen 200 px lower), but its task is on the right screen's panel
With the fix: same window position, the task stays on the left screen's panel
